item.title: RFK Jr. faces fierce backlash after US loses measles-free status for first time in 26 years
item.description: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. faces criticism after the U.S. lost measles elimination status amid over 5,400 confirmed cases this year.
item.content:encoded:
Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is facing mounting criticism from Democrats after the United States lost its measles elimination status for the first time in more than 25 years.

The Pan American Health Organization announced Tuesday that the U.S. had lost its measles elimination designation amid a resurgence of the highly contagious virus, with more than 5,400 confirmed cases reported this year — the highest annual total in more than three decades.

The virus has spread largely among unvaccinated populations, prompting criticism from Democrats who have previously scrutinized Kennedy's stance on vaccines.

On Tuesday, Kennedy vowed to stop measles outbreaks and restore the country's measles elimination status, while continuing to recommend vaccination against the disease.

CNN'S DANA BASH SPARS WITH RFK JR OVER VACCINE EFFICACY, DEMANDS HE 'LOOK INTO THE CAMERA' AND PUSH VACCINES

"We will stop measles outbreaks, protect American families, and work to regain U.S. measles elimination status," Kennedy said in a statement.

He added, "I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles."

Several Democrats sharply criticized Kennedy following the announcement.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, whose state has reported its first measles-associated death in more than three decades, involving a child, accused Kennedy of contributing to declining vaccination rates through years of vaccine skepticism.

CHILD’S MEASLES DEATH MARKS NEW YORK STATE’S FIRST IN MORE THAN 30 YEARS AMID OUTBREAK

"RFK Jr. promised to 'Make America Healthy Again.' Now America has lost its measles-free status for the first time in 26 years," Hochul said.

"A disgraceful display of incompetence from the nation's highest public health office," she added.

Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro also blamed Kennedy, arguing that the loss of elimination status reflected the consequences of vaccine misinformation and skepticism.

"There is a clear line from the misinformation, vaccine skepticism, and incompetence of RFK Jr. to this devastating news and very real consequences," Shapiro said.

"Measles is preventable. We eliminated it in this country once, and we can do it again."

MEASLES SURGE HITS NEW MILESTONE AS US CASES SURPASS LAST YEAR'S TOTAL

Another Democratic governor called for Kennedy's removal from office.

"This dangerous setback was 100% avoidable and is the result of one person: RFK Jr.," Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear said. "Remove him now."

The U.S., which had maintained the measles designation since 2000, is experiencing its worst measles outbreak since 1991 and has reported more than twice as many cases as in all of 2025, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Measles elimination means there has been no continuous local transmission of the virus for at least 12 months. The U.S. reached the status in 2000 after years of coordinated immunization campaigns.

NEW YORK DECLARES MEASLES DISASTER EMERGENCY AS CASES SURGE IN PENNSYLVANIA

CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz defended the agency's response to the ongoing outbreak, emphasizing that vaccination remains the most important tool for protecting Americans.

"The measles elimination designation is not what protects Americans. Vaccination does," Schwartz said.

She added that the CDC had invested approximately $100 million in state and local health departments to strengthen outbreak prevention and response.

The agency also noted that MMR vaccination coverage among U.S. kindergartners fell from 95.2% during the 2019–2020 school year to 92.7% in 2023–2024.

In his statement, Kennedy cited COVID-19-era disruptions as a factor in declining routine childhood vaccination coverage, noting that several other countries, including Canada, Mexico and the United Kingdom, had also lost their measles elimination status.

Fox News Digital has reached out to HHS for additional comment.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Patriots-Chargers game loses primetime slot as NFL makes first flex scheduling move of 2026 season
item.description: The NFL flexed the Las Vegas Raiders-Cleveland Browns game into "Sunday Night Football" for Week 12, bumping New England Patriots-Los Angeles Chargers.
item.content:encoded:
The Houston Texans will host the Indianapolis Colts to kick off Week 11 of the NFL slate. Week 12's lineup will look different than it did originally, as the league decided to make its first primetime shakeup on the calendar.

Although the Los Angeles Chargers picked up their first win Monday night in primetime, it was not enough to keep their Week 12 matchup with the New England Patriots in the Sunday night slot. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss the remainder of the season after breaking his ankle this past Sunday.

The Las Vegas Raiders-Cleveland Browns game is moving into the "Sunday Night Football" window for Nov. 29, the league announced on Tuesday.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The game will also be the Raiders’ first primetime appearance of the 2026 season and the first of rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza’s career. Mendoza is projected to make his third career start. Four other teams began the regular season without a primetime matchup on their schedules.

Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in April's draft, threw for 143 yards in his first career start. The defending champion Seahawks went on to win 21-13.

Last season, the Browns did not play any games on the national stage. They had one earlier this season, a Week 4 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

2026 NFL OROY ODDS: FERNANDO MENDOZA REMAINS FAVORITE

This season's surprising Browns enter their bye week at 6-4, showcasing their ability along the way to close out close games. There are several weeks left on the NFL schedule, but the Browns have already made league history by pulling off each of their first six wins by four points or fewer.

The Patriots-Chargers game moved to the late-afternoon window, while the AFC South matchup between the Tennessee Titans and Jacksonville Jaguars shifted to 1 p.m. ET after initially being scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET.

Nearly six years had passed since the Browns were last flexed into the Sunday night window. The last time it happened was on December 2020, when Cleveland faced the New York Giants. The Browns won that game and later clinched a playoff berth.

item.title: Alaska Dem Peltola defeats Sullivan, flipping 9th GOP Senate seat after 'decoy Dan' uproar
item.description: Democrats seized a 56-44 majority in the U.S. Senate after Mary Peltola defeated Alaska Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan in a race that featured a same-name ballot challenger.
item.content:encoded:
Democrats flipped a ninth GOP-held Senate seat in the 2026 midterm elections, with former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola defeating two-term Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan in a state that President Donald Trump carried in 2024.

Peltola's victory gives Democrats a 56-44 majority in the U.S. Senate.

The contest emerged as one of the nation's most closely watched Senate races, with Republicans defending a seat in a state President Donald Trump carried by roughly 13 percentage points in 2024, and Democrats eyeing a rare opportunity to make inroads in traditionally Republican territory.

The controversy deepened just days before Election Day when The New York Times reported that Peltola campaign aides, attorneys and national Democratic operatives had participated in a secret effort to recruit a candidate sharing the Republican incumbent's name.

According to the Times, text messages and interviews revealed a broader operation, internally dubbed the "ballot composition project," aimed at recruiting candidates who could siphon votes from Sullivan. The effort reportedly involved the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee and included discussions about establishing a new right-wing political party.

Peltola's campaign denied involvement with either Sullivan campaign, while the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) also rejected allegations of participation. The revelations prompted Republican Gov. Michael Dunleavy to order an investigation into whether the alleged recruitment effort violated Alaska law.

The Cook Political Report rated the contest a toss-up, reflecting the unusually competitive environment in a state that has generally favored Republicans in federal elections.

Peltola, a former state lawmaker, made history in 2022 when she became the first Alaska Native elected to Congress, winning a special election to succeed the late Republican Rep. Don Young.

GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING

She defeated former Republican Gov. Sarah Palin in that contest before winning a full term later that year. Peltola subsequently lost her 2024 reelection bid to Republican Nick Begich III, setting the stage for her Senate campaign.

Sullivan, a Marine Corps veteran and former Alaska attorney general, first won his Senate seat in 2014 by defeating Democratic incumbent Mark Begich, Nick's uncle. He secured reelection in 2020 and sought a third term emphasizing his experience, national security and Alaska's energy interests.

The 2026 race also featured an unusual ballot controversy involving Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher who shared nearly the same name as the Republican incumbent.

Alaska election officials initially moved to remove the second Sullivan from the ballot amid allegations that his candidacy was intended to confuse voters or siphon support from the senator. The candidate denied wrongdoing, and the Alaska Supreme Court ruled that he could remain on the ballot. The DOJ sued in October to mitigate any "misleading" impact of the newcomer Sullivan.

COURT KEEPS ‘DECOY DAN’ ON ALASKA BALLOT AS EXPERT WARNS RANKED-CHOICE SYSTEM CREATES VOTER ‘TRAPS’

The controversy added another complication to Alaska's ranked-choice voting system, which allows voters to rank candidates in order of preference.

Under the system, a candidate receiving a majority of first-choice votes wins outright. Otherwise, the lowest-performing candidate is eliminated, and ballots are redistributed according to voters' next available preferences until a winner emerges.

Peltola had previously benefited from the system during her 2022 congressional victories, when ranked-choice tabulation helped determine the outcomes of races featuring multiple Republican opponents.

The Alaska contest carried national significance as both parties battled over control of the Senate, with the result determining whether Republicans retained the seat or Democrats added it to their column.

item.title: College Football Playoff Rankings: Texas rewarded for thrilling win vs LSU, Georgia remains top dog
item.description: Arch Manning led a game-winning drive past the Tigers as Texas jumped to No. 5 in the College Football Playoff rankings, with Georgia holding at No. 1.
item.content:encoded:
The College Football Playoff committee has released its third iteration of rankings, and unlike the previous two, there isn’t much movement going on near the top.

Curt Cignetti and the reigning national-champion Indiana Hoosiers may have wanted some teams above them at No. 9 to lose, but all eight managed a victory.

So, how would the CFP committee view those wins in terms of movement?

The top four remained the same, as Georgia stays atop the throne at No. 1, followed by No. 2 Utah, who staved off Arizona in a 40-39 thriller to remain undefeated, No. 3 Alabama, who had an interesting time in Nashville against Vanderbilt while other ranked teams they’ve beaten lost, and No. 4 UCLA, who defeated a good Illinois squad.

However, we have a new team at No. 5, with Arch Manning and Texas swapping places with Notre Dame from last week’s rankings, and it has everything to do with yet another ranked-opponent victory.

It was cinema in Death Valley, as Manning led a game-winning touchdown drive to beat the Tigers, 22-21, and the CFP committee rewarded them for it. Texas has five wins in the top 25, the most of any team in the field, and it’s been clear this committee favors who you’ve beaten rather than who you’ve lost to.

Just look at Arizona, who took the undefeated Utes down to the wire, but came away with its third loss of the year. But they went from No. 23 in last week’s rankings to No. 19, which is a CFP record in terms of spots moved after a loss.

With Notre Dame and Miami at No. 6 and 7 respectively, we saw Indiana, coming off a statement win over a ranked USC Trojans squad, move into the No. 8 slot. Tennessee feel one spot to No. 9, while BYU rounded out the top 10.

Cignetti stated earlier this week that he doesn’t care to hear about the strength of Indiana’s schedule, but the committee clearly saw an offense they have been dying to see that resulted in one spot up the board, which would give the Hoosiers a home playoff game if the season ended today.

"What we were really impressed with as a committee was what Indiana did as an offense," CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek told ESPN’s Rece Davis. " … That’s the thing that had been missing from Indiana this year."

Finally, Wake Forest would be the last team in today at No. 11 with a 9-1 record, while Texas Tech would be the first team out at No. 12 due to the Group of 6 team, Boise State, who came in at No. 17 after jumping seven spots this week, needing a spot in the bracket.

But it’s interesting to see two three-loss teams from the Big Ten, Oregon at No. 13 and Ohio State at No. 14, on the bubble and very much in the mix over the next couple of weeks. The Buckeyes particularly looked dead after back-to-back losses gave them three total on the year.

item.title: Mamdani's luxury second home tax hits $500M milestone despite thousands of exemptions
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani's pied-à-terre tax has billed wealthy second-home owners more than $500 million, even as tax bills fell far below initial estimates.
item.content:encoded:
New York City has billed wealthy second-home owners more than $500 million under Mayor Zohran Mamdani's controversial pied-à-terre tax, even as the number of homeowners receiving bills fell far below initial estimates.

"We've billed more than $500 million to owners of second homes worth more than $5 million," Mamdani wrote Tuesday on X.

"That's half a billion dollars to invest in a City that works for all New Yorkers," he continued.

According to information provided by city officials, the New York City Department of Finance mailed approximately 7,500 tax bills — a sizable drop from the roughly 17,000 initial notices sent to property owners over the summer.

APPEALS COURT HANDS MAMDANI LEGAL WIN ON NYC LUXURY SECOND-HOME TAX

Officials also said roughly 8,900 exemption applications were granted, while approximately 1,600 extension applications were denied.

The surcharge is a key part of the mayor's agenda to raise taxes on wealthy New Yorkers and help close the city's budget gap.

Despite the smaller number of bills, the city said the total amount billed exceeded the $500 million target previously outlined by Gov. Kathy Hochul earlier this year.

However, officials did not immediately provide a breakdown showing how the total was calculated across the approximately 7,500 properties.

"As Mayor Mamdani has said before, owning a second home worth over 5 million dollars should come with a responsibility to the city that makes it valuable," Julia Agos, a spokesperson for the Department of Finance, said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"The Department of Finance will continue to implement the pied-a-terre surcharge fairly and efficiently, ensuring that those most able to contribute do their part to build a city that works for everyone," Agos added.

The tax is assessed on a sliding scale based on property values, meaning owners of more expensive homes can face higher charges.

JIM GAFFIGAN, NEW YORK LAWMAKERS PUSH GOV HOCHUL TO AXE 'UNNECESSARY TAX' HITTING COMEDY CLUBS

In an April report, the New York City comptroller's office estimated that a version of the tax could generate approximately $500 million from more than 11,200 properties before accounting for exemptions and changes in homeowner behavior.

After accounting for those factors, however, the report projected that revenue could fall to between roughly $340 million and $380 million.

Still, Mamdani has continued to express confidence in the surcharge's revenue potential, telling reporters last week, "We continue to be confident in its ability to raise half a billion dollars per year."

The surcharge, approved by the New York state Legislature in May, applies to qualifying luxury second homes in New York City, including certain one- to three-family properties valued at $5 million or more and condos and co-ops valued at $1 million or more.

MAMDANI WARNING TO WEALTHY NEW YORKERS ABOUT 'FAIR SHARE' SPARKS ONLINE FIRESTORM: 'FULL BLOWN COMMUNIST'

Property owners who qualify for exemptions are not subject to the surcharge.

Tuesday's announcement comes after a state appeals court handed Mamdani a legal victory earlier this month, unanimously dismissing a lawsuit challenging the rollout of the surcharge.

The court found that the homeowners who brought the lawsuit lacked legal standing, overturning a lower court ruling that had ordered the city to restart implementation.

However, the tax continues to face separate legal challenges, including questions about its constitutionality.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the mayor's office for comment.

Fox News Digital's Brittany Miller contributed to this report.

item.title: Ken Griffin, target of Zohran Mamdani, has officially sold his $58 million apartment to NY Jets owner
item.description: Ken Griffin says NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani's pied-à-terre tax pushed him to double down on Miami, selling an apartment to Jets owner Woody Johnson.
item.content:encoded:
You gotta hand it to Zohran Mamdani. He may not be smart, competent or honest, but he is extremely capable of pushing people out of New York City.

The current mayor of New York, who's spent his time in office purposefully looking for ways to make life in the city worse, made it one of his top priorities to try and punish wealthy residents who own second homes there. That punishment, short-sighted and nonsensical as it is, focused on taking money from those with properties in the city that aren't main residences with his so-called "pied-à-terre" tax.

Mamdani's campaign of absurdity started earlier in 2026 by directly targeting one of the wealthiest people in the country, billionaire hedge fund manager Ken Griffin, CEO of Citadel. Griffin has created thousands of jobs in New York, contributing untold billions to the local economy. He also had plans to build a $6 billion office building in Manhattan to supplant his firm's new headquarters in Miami.

'WE'RE TAXING THE RICH': NYC MAYOR MAMDANI TOUTS NEW $500M-A-YEAR TAX ON LUXURY SECOND HOMES

You'd think that the mayor of a major city would want to work and partner with someone of such influence who can help local residents and generate immensely valuable careers and investments. Mamdani, brilliant as he is, decided instead to make an example of him.

In one of his typically cringe-inducing social media videos meant to appeal to his uninformed voters and supporters, Mamdani in April 2026 went in front of a camera and pointed out Griffin's apartment. Immediately, it backfired.

Speaking at a conference not long afterward, Griffin described the video as "creepy" as well as potentially dangerous.

"And then the second time you’re like, you know what this is? Actually, this has gone from creepy to actually not really creepy, this has gone frightening."

"The CEO of UnitedHealthcare was killed just a few blocks from my house," he explained.

NBA STAR RIPS SOCIALIST NYC MAYOR ZOHRAN MAMDANI AS 'MAYOR PLAYING PRESIDENT' AFTER NETANYAHU VIDEO

"And anything that creates, like an agitation of the extremists on either side of the aisle is a frightening dynamic."

It's unclear whether Griffin found Mamdani's videos or his fake smile more creepy.

Then, when asked about the potential office building, he said that Citadel was reevaluating and discussing their options, as well as committing to further expansion in Miami.

"The mayor of New York has made clear to my partners and principally my New York partners...that we need to double down on our bet in Miami because we want to be in a state that embraces, business, that embraces education, that embraces personal freedom and liberty, and that embraces people having an opportunity to live the American Dream and a dream of earned success, not a dream of redistributive handouts that leave people dependent on government for their lives," Griffin said.

And while he retains the apartment targeted in Mamdani's video, he's now sold an another apartment, to New York Jets owner Woody Johnson, to avoid Mamdani's taxes moving forward.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

"I wish Woody and his family many happy years in one of New York’s great residences," he said in a quote to The New York Post on Tuesday.

Griffin hasn't totally exited the city, since he still owns real estate there, but it's a sign of how Mamdani's ridiculous policies and public persona have real consequences for New York. Not to mention how naive and simplistic his thinking is. "Just tax the rich," he says, somehow thinking that rich people can't simply leave or sell instead of dealing with him and higher costs.

Not to mention the ancillary issues. All that tax revenue Mamdani budgets for dries up if these wealthy individuals leave. Then there's potential investment and future jobs and businesses that move away or never start because of the anti-capitalist mindset currently running the city. If Mamdani were a sane, rational person, you'd expect him to learn from this. But he isn't, and won't. He never will.

item.title: Major drug kingpin ‘The Kraken’ captured in California after yearslong hunt
item.description: Alleged Guatemalan cocaine kingpin Axel Montejo Saenz, known as "Kraken," was arrested in San Diego after agents seized over 5,500 kilograms of cocaine, authorities said.
item.content:encoded:
An alleged Guatemalan cocaine kingpin known as "Kraken" has been arrested in San Diego, and federal officials are offering up to $10 million for information that could lead to his conviction.

Axel Bladimir Montejo Saenz, 40, is accused of helping run a cocaine trafficking network with ties to narcoterrorist cartels.

Agents seized more than 5,500 kilograms of cocaine and $3.7 million linked to him during a yearslong investigation, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California.

EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE TRUMP'S CARTEL CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE OFFICIAL DETAILS PRESIDENT'S PRIVATE BRIEFINGS

"Every drug kingpin has an expiration date. Today was his," U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon said in a statement Monday.

The State Department also announced a separate reward of up to $10 million for information leading to the arrest or conviction of Walfre Donaldo Calderon-Calderon, 44, known as "El Teniente Jr." Prosecutors say he leads a drug trafficking operation in northwestern Guatemala near the Mexican border.

EXCLUSIVE: FBI EXTRADITIONS SOAR AS PATEL RAMPS UP FOREIGN OUTREACH, VOWS 'NO SANCTUARY'

Montejo Saenz pleaded not guilty Nov. 9 in federal court in San Diego. Members of the Homeland Security Task Force arrested him on charges that he conspired to distribute cocaine bound for the United States and to distribute cocaine aboard a vessel. He faces up to life in prison if convicted.

Prosecutors allege the operation moved cocaine through at least six countries, including Colombia, Ecuador, Guatemala and Mexico, and continued through November 2018. The U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned Montejo Saenz and the Los Huistas drug trafficking organization in 2022.

DRUG CARTEL KINGPIN AMONG TARGETS IN SWEEPING TRUMP CRACKDOWN ON ALLEGED MEXICAN CORRUPTION NETWORK

Calderon-Calderon was indicted in 2019 on two cocaine conspiracy charges. Prosecutors said his indictment was unsealed in June 2025 after a deadly shootout involving Mexican law enforcement in Huehuetenango, Guatemala.

5 MEXICAN CARTEL BOSSES CHARGED IN WEAPONS, DRUG TRAFFICKING, TIMESHARE FRAUD SCHEMES, DOJ SAYS

Federal agents received information that his father, Baldemar Calderon-Carrillo, known as "Don Valde" and the lead defendant in the case, was killed in the gunfight, the U.S. Attorney’s Office said.

The two rewards follow the April arrest of another alleged Guatemalan drug kingpin, Eugenio Dario Molina-Lopez, known as "Don Dario." The State Department had offered up to $10 million for information leading to his arrest or conviction in 2022.

item.title: Former Yankees slugger Mark Teixeira celebrates as Congress’s version of Mr Irrelevant at office lottery
item.description: Mark Teixeira drew chip No. 105 of 105 in the House freshman office lottery, earning Congress's "Mr. Irrelevant" tag and a playful un-victory lap.
item.content:encoded:
Retired MLB slugger Mark Teixeira began his baseball career sitting at the top of the draft boards, so Washington wasted no time humbling him Tuesday.

Incoming members of Congress have zero seniority, so they draw numbers from a box to set the draft order for picking Capitol Hill offices. On Tuesday, the newly elected Texas Republican pulled chip No. 105 out of 105, giving every other rookie first dibs while leaving him with the scraps.

Even with the dead-last pick, Teixeira hopped on X to voice how happy he was to earn the spot.

"I consider it an honor to have the last pick of offices and let all my fellow freshmen go ahead of me," the ex-New York Yankee posted.

Finishing dead last makes Teixeira Congress's version of "Mr. Irrelevant," leaving him with whatever leftover office nobody else wants for the next two years.

DEMOCRATS FACE DAUNTING CONGRESSIONAL BASEBALL GAME STREAK AS EX-MLB GREAT EYES GOP ROSTER SPOT

But Teixeira handled it like a vet.

His draw sparked cheers and a bipartisan standing ovation, so Teixeira took a playful "un-victory lap" around the room, jogging past new colleagues and trading high-fives and fistbumps.

"Sometimes you prepare, you put the work in, and it’s just not your night," Teixeira told reporters afterward.

FROM LOCKER ROOMS TO CONGRESS: JAY FEELY LATEST ATHLETE SEEKING TO TAKE LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP TO CAPITOL HILL

Being picked dead last is new territory for a guy the Texas Rangers drafted fifth overall in 2001. Over 14 MLB seasons, Teixeira crushed 409 home runs, won five Gold Gloves, made three All-Star games, and captured a 2009 World Series ring in New York.

After retiring in 2016, Teixeira worked at ESPN before jumping into Texas politics.

In August 2025, he launched a Republican run for Texas’s open 21st Congressional District, promising to fight "for the principles that make Texas strong and America exceptional."

EX-YANKEE MARK TEIXEIRA UNLOADS ON MLB FOR TRYING TO 'SILENCE' CHRISTIAN FAITH

With President Trump's endorsement, Teixeira cruised through his March primary and beat Democrat Kristin Hook on November 3 with 55% of the vote.

"Tonight’s victory belongs to the people of Texas’s 21st District," Teixeira said on election night. "I’m not going to Washington for myself, but rather to be a strong, responsive voice for every family in this district." He will just have to make that voice heard from the worst office in D.C.

item.title: New lawsuit alleges AI app 'Bron' used LeBron James’ tattoos, voice and jersey to promote sports-betting tool
item.description: LeBron James alleges an AI sports-betting app called "Bron" faked his endorsement, with its ad viewed about 1 million times before it was taken down.
item.content:encoded:
LeBron James filed a lawsuit Tuesday against the developers of an AI sports-betting app, accusing the company of violating his publicity rights and trademarks by branding the product "Bron" and using AI-generated images of him in marketing materials.

The lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court in New York, claims the developers used James’ name, likeness and nickname without permission to promote an otherwise unknown product. James’ attorneys described the alleged conduct as "a willful, bad-faith tactic" designed to capitalize on the 76ers star’s fame.

The complaint asks the court to bar the developers from using James’ name, surrender any resulting profits and pay damages, including the fair-market value of its alleged use and punitive damages.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Defendants did not care that they had engaged in illegal conduct to gain notoriety for their previously unknown app," the lawsuit read. "They intentionally created the false impression that Mr. James endorsed and was affiliated with their Bron App, in an effort to drive downloads and paid subscriptions."

PlayVision Inc., the California-based developer of the app, was launched in 2025 by CEO Anish Gupta and CTO Marc Zoghby with backing from startup accelerator Y Combinator. The company developed a platform that uses artificial intelligence to analyze game and practice footage for sports teams and fans.

LEBRON JAMES SENDS CEASE AND DESIST TO 'BRON AI' SPORTS BETTING APP OVER UNAUTHORIZED LIKENESS

PlayVision launched the "Bron" app this year, saying it does not accept wagers directly but charges a subscription fee for features such as bet tracking and odds comparisons. A marketing campaign this month depicted a person resembling James, complete with similar tattoos, voice and No. 23 jersey, using the app in a locker room.

Messages sent by OutKick through the app’s website seeking comment were not immediately returned Tuesday.

A spokesperson for James previously confirmed that his lawyers sent the company a cease-and-desist letter. PlayVision removed the ad, but not before it was reposted and viewed roughly 1 million times, according to the lawsuit.

"I’m sure the intent here was for us to send a cease and desist in order to make it a story," James' longtime media advisor Adam Mendelsohn told Front Office Sports. "You would prefer not to respond but you don’t have a choice in a situation like this. It’s not the first time and it won’t be the last. For what it’s worth, these gimmicks never work because people see through it."

LEBRON JAMES SAYS 'MY FAMILY IS SAFE' AFTER MAN CAUGHT ON GROUNDS OF HIS LOS ANGELES HOME

Gupta responded to the attorneys’ demand on social media by writing that the app would get a new name, but no new name had been adopted by the time the lawsuit was filed, leading James’ legal team to suggest the company was milking the controversy for attention. Gupta wrote on social media this week that the new name will be announced Wednesday.

The lawsuit notes that James typically commands tens of millions of dollars for such endorsement deals, and that he already has an exclusive deal with the prediction market platform Polymarket. It alleges that the app’s marketing was especially harmful in part because it showed the AI-generated James scrolling through bets involving NBA players.

James left the Los Angeles Lakers after eight seasons this offseason and joined the Philadelphia 76ers. Through 15 games of the 2026-27 season, Philadelphia’s 12 wins lead the Eastern Conference. James’ former team also has 12 wins and is tied with the San Antonio Spurs atop the Western Conference.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Pope Leo breaks silence on rosary striking his face in Peru, reveals details about cancer: 'Major surgery'
item.description: Pope Leo XIV says his lung cancer was found in a routine check-up with no symptoms, crediting prayer and doctors for his recovery before the Peru trip.
item.content:encoded:
Pope Leo XIV broke his silence Monday after being struck in the face by a rosary thrown by a worshipper in Peru, joking about the incident while also revealing details for the very first time about his cancer diagnosis and major surgery which took place before his recent trip to South America.

The pope, who had the lower lobe of his right lung removed Oct. 13, after doctors found a cancerous tumor, told reporters on the flight home to Rome that he has not fully recovered, but said he was determined to complete the long-planned 12-day journey.

"Just over a month ago, as everybody knows, I underwent rather major surgery," Leo, 71, said during a roughly 45-minute news conference on board the papal plane returning from Lima, Peru.

POPE LEO WELCOMED BACK AS HE DELIVERS ANGELUS PRAYER DAYS AFTER LUNG CANCER SURGERY

"But from the very beginning, I had in mind that this trip had been planned and that I was going to make it happen."

The pontiff credited his recovery to prayer, medical care and personal determination.

"So, with God's help — and I firmly believe in the power of prayer, as I have literally received messages from all over the world — together with a certain personal determination, which I also have, and with the help of the doctors, it proved to be possible."

Despite the demanding itinerary that included multiple flights and appearances before massive crowds in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, Leo acknowledged that he is still regaining his strength.

POPE LEO XIV SEEN FOR FIRST TIME SINCE LUNG CANCER SURGERY AMID MAJOR RECOVERY MILESTONE

"I must say that I am not at 100%, but I am doing quite well. Stamina is a gift I have received from the Lord," he said.

The pope also revealed that his cancer diagnosis came as a shock after doctors found an abnormality during a routine annual medical examination.

"The initial news came as a surprise. There were no symptoms — I felt fine," he said.

"It was discovered during some medical tests, as part of what you might call a check-up: a routine annual examination that I have been having for many years."

Leo said the abnormality initially appeared as a shadow on his lung before additional testing revealed a tumor.

POPE LEO UNDERGOES BLOOD TESTS, X-RAY FOLLOWING CANCER SURGERY, VATICAN SAYS

"A biopsy then confirmed that it was a tumor," he said, before adding that he had decided to get it done "right away."

"By the grace of God, I remained calm," he added.

The surgery removed the lower lobe of his right lung after doctors diagnosed lung adenocarcinoma, a type of lung cancer. The pope was discharged four days later.

"No further treatment is necessary. However, as a precaution, I will need to continue having these routine check-ups, simply to keep an eye on things, as is normal," he explained.

The Vatican cleared the pontiff to move forward with his South American trip after medical evaluations in late October.

The journey, which began Nov. 6, marked Leo's first papal visit to Latin America. He also holds Peruvian citizenship and spent roughly two decades serving as a missionary and bishop in Peru before taking on leadership roles at the Vatican.

POPE LEO XIV HIT IN THE FACE BY FLYING ROSARY DURING FAREWELL MASS IN PERU, VIDEO SHOWS

It was while riding in the popemobile through huge crowds toward the Mass in Lima on Nov. 16 that Leo was struck near the eye by a rosary thrown from the crowd.

"The affection shown by the Peruvian people, including the person who, with such great faith, simply wanted to offer me a rosary, is something one carries in one's heart — or perhaps in one's eye," he joked about the incident.

"These are experiences that leave a lasting mark on one's life."

"They bear witness to genuine enthusiasm, deep faith, and the desire to receive the Lord's blessing," he added before describing the crowds' devotion.

"Some even tried to get past the National Police barricades. They simply wanted to live, feel, and experience this faith," he said.

item.title: Pentagon sued by The Intercept, Freedom of the Press Foundation over alleged 'blacklist' of news outlets
item.description: The Freedom of the Press Foundation and The Intercept sued the Pentagon over an alleged journalist blacklist, citing a CENTCOM warning to journalist Nick Turse.
item.content:encoded:
The Pentagon is being sued over an alleged "blacklist" of journalists and news outlets maintained by the Trump administration.

The lawsuit, filed Monday by the nonprofit Freedom of the Press Foundation (FPF) and The Intercept in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., stems from a July interaction between The Intercept reporter Nick Turse and the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) public affairs office regarding Iran's attacks on U.S. bases in the Middle East.

After making repeated phone calls and receiving no answers, Turse was warned by CENTCOM public affairs executive assistant Richard Allee he would be "put on a list of people to disregard" if he didn't stop pursuing the story.

"Turse asked for clarification: 'You have a list of people to disregard?' Allee confirmed with an emphatic: 'Yes,'" the lawsuit states. Turse asked which reporters or outlets were currently on the list. Allee replied, 'I’m not privy to give you that information.' Turse asked if it was a secret list, and Allee stated 'it's not a list that we publicize' before hanging up the phone."

FIRED STARS AND STRIPES STAFFERS SUE PENTAGON, ALLEGE RETALIATION AND FIRST AMENDMENT VIOLATION

Turse later reported in August that he had spoken with an unnamed U.S. official who told him that the office of Secretary of War Pete Hegseth "had a standing order not to engage with" him, according to the lawsuit.

In August, both Turse and FPF filed Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests to seek Pentagon documents pertaining to journalists and news organizations who are on the alleged "blacklist." 

CENTCOM has not responded to the requests, according to the lawsuit.

The suit accuses the Pentagon of two counts of "unlawful withholding of agency records by statutory deadline."

PRESS FREEDOM GROUPS THAT BLASTED TRUMP TURN FIRE ON DEM GOVERNOR OVER ALLEGED MEDIA RETALIATION

Lauren Harper, FPF's Ellsberg chair on government secrecy, who filed the FOIA request on the group's behalf, told Fox News Digital allegations of blacklisted reporters "should concern both sides of the political aisle because the tactics that may be used to silence left-leaning outlets today, could be turned on right-leaning ones tomorrow."

"The Pentagon’s budget is at an all-time high, and taxpayers have a right to know how that money is being spent — especially when questions arise about the legality of its operations and potentially dangerous living conditions of its troops," Harper said. 

"It is the job of an independent press to ask tough questions about these issues and more, regardless of who is in the White House or who runs the Pentagon."

Turse called the existence of a journalist blacklist "fundamentally un-American."

"The Pentagon is keeping vital information secret from Congress and the public — including the true toll of the Iran War," Turse told Fox News Digital. "The American people have a right to know how many service members and civilians have been injured or killed. 

"They also deserve to know the economic costs of the conflict. But the public isn't getting answers because the Pentagon stonewalls and obfuscates. They didn’t want to answer hard questions, so they threatened to blacklist me.

"If they can do it to me, they can do it to other journalists who demand the truth," he added. "This is a disservice to military personnel and the wider public. If the Defense Department won’t come clean about the war, we’ll compel them in court." 

NEW YORK TIMES BLASTS ‘ABUSIVE’ TRUMP SUBPOENAS TARGETING REPORTERS’ SOURCES

CENTCOM previously denied having a blacklist and called Turse’s account "a complete misrepresentation of exchanges that occurred." It also accused him of repeatedly harassing its staff.

A spokesperson for the Pentagon declined to comment to Fox News Digital. The Intercept did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: White House pulls Trump’s FDA pick Heidi Overton on eve of Senate panel vote
item.description: President Donald Trump's FDA pick, Heidi Overton, saw her nomination pulled one day before a Senate committee vote, a White House official confirmed.
item.content:encoded:
The White House pulled Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead the Food and Drug Administration, a White House official confirmed to Fox News, one day before a Senate committee vote.

President Donald Trump hailed Overton as a "ROCKSTAR" in August when he picked the physician and White House advisor to succeed Marty Makary, who resigned in May.

At her September confirmation hearing, Overton clashed with Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., as he pressed her to endorse universal healthcare as a human right.

TRUMP TO NOMINATE DR HEIDI OVERTON AS NEXT FDA COMMISSIONER

Senate health committee Chairman Bill Cassidy, R-La., pointed to Overton’s appearance alongside Trump in the Oval Office as Trump signed an executive order calling for changes to childhood vaccine recommendations, including splitting up the combined measles, mumps and rubella vaccine.

Cassidy said there was no scientific evidence for Trump’s suggestion that the combined shot could be "quite lethal" and warned the remark could discourage vaccination.

TRUMP SURGEON GENERAL PICK BACKS MMR VACCINE, REJECTS LINK BETWEEN CHILDHOOD VACCINES AND AUTISM

"Yes, Senator, the MMR vaccine is safe and effective," Overton told Cassidy. When he pressed her on what she would do if Trump asked her to disregard the FDA’s safety standards, Overton said she would give the president her best advice and follow the legal requirements for reviewing individual products.

Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., asked Overton directly whether Trump was wrong. Overton reiterated that the vaccine was safe and effective and called it the best tool available during the measles outbreak. Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., questioned why she hadn’t corrected Trump in the Oval Office.

NEW YORK DECLARES MEASLES DISASTER EMERGENCY AS CASES SURGE IN PENNSYLVANIA

"So why should we expect you to stand up to the president as FDA commissioner?" Markey asked.

Overton worked on several of the administration’s Make America Healthy Again initiatives as a White House advisor.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS EMBRACE HEALTH AGENDA WHILE RATING RFK JR NEGATIVELY

Before returning to the White House, she served as vice chair and chief policy officer at the conservative America First Policy Institute, where she criticized expanded access to abortion pills in a 2023 policy brief.

Kyle Diamantas has led the agency in an acting capacity since Makary’s departure.

PRO-LIFE CEO PREDICTS TRUMP FDA NOMINEE COULD BRING RENEWED SCRUTINY TO ABORTION DRUG RISKS

Erik Baptist, senior vice president for legal strategy at SBA Pro-Life America, said the group wants the next FDA nominee to commit to ending mail-order access to abortion drugs and changing how the agency studies their safety before the Senate holds a confirmation vote.

MAJOR PRO-LIFE GROUP THREATENS TO SUE TRUMP FDA OVER ABORTION PILL'S ALLEGED ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS

"The administration must immediately end the Biden FDA’s mail-order abortion-drug scheme and protect pregnant women from predators who coerce or poison women with these drugs," Baptist said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "And the FDA must fix its flawed safety study by obtaining robust data, increasing real-time transparency, and inviting external experts to help with this study."

"Confirmation is not a coronation," he added. "It is a time to vet nominees and seek commitments before they take office."

Fox News’ Pat Ward, Caroline McKee, and James Cirrone contributed to this report.

item.title: Kim Jong Un's daughter hits ski slopes in rare photos as North Korean dictator tours mountain resort
item.description: Kim Jong Un watched from a throne-like chair, cigarette in hand, as his daughter Kim Ju Ae skied down a snowy North Korean resort during a family outing.
item.content:encoded:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was photographed sitting in an ornate, throne-like armchair in the middle of a snowy ski resort while his daughter, viewed as his likely successor, carved down the slopes during an unusual family outing.

The striking images, released Monday by North Korean state media, show Kim wearing sunglasses and dress shoes while seated in the elaborate upholstered chair, holding a lit cigarette.

Other photographs show his daughter skiing in an all-white outfit as officials navigate the slopes nearby.

The girl, believed to be named Kim Ju Ae, has increasingly appeared alongside her father at high-profile public events. 

South Korea's National Intelligence Service has assessed that she is being positioned as his likely successor, although North Korea has not publicly confirmed a succession plan.

TRUMP ARRIVES IN PHILIPPINES AHEAD OF XI JINPING SUMMIT IN CHINA AFTER GOP MIDTERM LOSSES

The snowy spectacle unfolded just as President Donald Trump raised the possibility that Kim could make an unexpected appearance during his upcoming high-stakes meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"We might have Kim Jong Un. He may come, I don't know. That's up to President Xi," Trump told reporters Monday.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump was serious about potentially meeting Kim, though no talks were confirmed.

"If we have a problem with North Korea, the only way we're ever going to solve it is if we engage with them," Rubio told reporters in the Philippines, adding that a meeting "may not happen."

TRUMP’S ASIA TRIP TAKES ALASKA DETOUR AS WEATHER FORCES REFUELING STOP CHANGE

The photographs were taken during Kim's Nov. 15–16 inspection of a tourist zone under development in Samjiyon, a mountainous city in northern North Korea, according to a report by the state-run Pyongyang Times reviewed by Fox News Digital.

Kim visited a ski resort under construction near Mount Pukphothae, where he examined skiing tracks and equipment and instructed officials to prepare the facilities for operation, the outlet reported.

His daughter was photographed skiing at the tourist zone on Nov. 15, according to an Associated Press caption accompanying the government-provided images.

The North Korean leader's visit was part of a broader effort to transform Samjiyon into a year-round mountain tourism destination, with plans for hotels, ski facilities, railway connections and an expanded airport.

TRUMP PLAYS NUCLEAR POKER WITH KIM JONG UN — BUT WHO HOLDS THE CARDS?

The appearance of Kim's daughter added another layer of intrigue to the ski resort visit.

South Korean intelligence officials have pointed to her increasingly prominent public role as evidence that she may eventually inherit power from her father. In an October 2026, assessment reported by KBS World, the National Intelligence Service said her position as a potential successor was strengthening.

The agency has also noted her frequent appearances at military-related events, although the North Korean government has made no formal announcement identifying her as the country's next leader.

The latest photographs offered a different setting for the young girl, showing her navigating a groomed ski slope rather than accompanying her father at an official event.

Meanwhile, the possibility of renewed diplomacy between Trump and Kim remains uncertain.

Trump and Kim last met in 2019, when their summit in Hanoi ended without an agreement on North Korea's nuclear program. Efforts to restart negotiations have since stalled as Pyongyang has continued developing its nuclear and missile capabilities.

A U.S. official told ABC News last week that no engagement with North Korea was planned during Trump's Asia trip, according to Fox News Digital's previous reporting.

Fox News Digital's Alec Schemmel contributed to this reporting.

item.title: 'Mob Wives' star Renee Graziano rejects NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani as 'not my choice' in public safety clash
item.description: Former "Mob Wives" star Renee Graziano criticized NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani and criminal justice policies on Tomi Lahren's podcast, as Mamdani defended his NYPD overhaul.
item.content:encoded:
Former "Mob Wives" star Renee Graziano criticized New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a discussion on public safety, saying he is "not my choice."

Speaking on the "Tomi Lahren Is Fearless" podcast, Graziano told Lahren that Americans shouldn’t be attacked for wanting their streets to be safe and said she disagrees with Mamdani on "probably everything."

"I don't agree with him on a lot of things. Probably everything, I don't agree with him," Graziano said. "He's not my choice. And if he is for other people, God bless them. He would not be the person I voted for."

Graziano’s comments came after Lahren raised concerns about New York’s no-cash bail policies and Mamdani’s move to disband the NYPD’s protest unit.

Under changes announced by Mamdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch on Monday dissolving the Strategic Response Group (SRG), the unit’s counterterrorism functions will be folded into the Intelligence and Counterterrorism Bureau, while a new civilian-led Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD) and specialized NYPD teams will handle protest response.

MICHAEL RUIZ: NEW YORK'S GUTTED POLICE UNIT WAS MORE THAN A PROTEST SQUAD

Graziano, who said she tries "not to pay attention" to Mamdani, criticized the justice system, arguing that criminal justice policies have allowed repeat offenders to be released.

"You're letting men out that raped women, and they get out and they rape women. They're out the door 20 seconds later, and they're still committing crimes," she said.

Graziano said she’s faced criticism on social media for calling for public safety, including being labeled "MAGA" by commenters.

"I had made a statement. One day on my Instagram, I said, ‘Can we make America safe again?’ And I got attacked viciously," Graziano said.

"‘Oh, you're a MAGA, you're this, you're that, you're Trumper,’ or you're this or that," Graziano added. "First of all, who I decide to pick is my business. I don't need to tell anybody, it's my choice. But I would never attack a person because they don't like this color or they don't like that. I would never do that. And I've experienced that across the board. And all I said was make it safe. I didn't say make it great. I said, make it safe."

JIM CAVIEZEL SAYS A SURREAL ENCOUNTER WITH JESUS CONVINCED HIM TO STAR IN 'THE PASSION OF THE CHRIST'

Graziano also argued that Americans need to be fully committed to the country, saying those who don't want to be here "can leave."

"You know, don’t half step in America. We are America. We are a beautiful country. So either we're all in or we're out. And if you don't want to be here, you can leave. That's how I truly feel."

At a news conference Tuesday, Mamdani defended his decision to dissolve the SRG, describing counterterrorism and protest response as "fundamentally different responsibilities."

MAMDANI PREPARES TO FULFILL PROMISE TO AXE NYPD UNIT RESPONSIBLE FOR CONTROLLING PROTEST VIOLENCE

"New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat. I made this promise over the course of the campaign, and I'm proud to be fulfilling this promise," Mamdani said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani's team for comment but did not immediately hear back.

Fox News Digital’s Anders Hagstrom contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump administration permanently pulls funding from LA homeless agency over mounting fraud allegations
item.description: The Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority will give up about $150 million in federal funding under a HUD settlement, with LA County managing the money.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration on Monday announced a landmark settlement to permanently cut the scandal-plagued Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA) off from federal funding, citing overwhelming evidence of fraud and years of mismanagement that wasted taxpayer dollars.

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) said the agreement requires LAHSA to relinquish about $150 million in federal funding and permanently sever its ties to HUD's homelessness funding programs by the end of 2027.

"Organizations that are complicit in this fraud and waste will not get one penny more of federal funding," Bill Essayli, first assistant U.S. attorney for the Central District of California, said in a statement.

LA HOMELESSNESS FRAUD CASES EXPOSE DEEPER PROBLEM THAN STOLEN MILLIONS, OVERSIGHT HAWK WARNS

Los Angeles County will take over managing the funds used to combat homelessness, while HUD will closely monitor how the money is spent, according to officials.

The agreement, executed Thursday, resolves a lawsuit filed by LAHSA challenging HUD's June decision to suspend further funding to the agency.

According to HUD, investigators found that LAHSA received more federal homelessness funding than any other jurisdiction in the nation, taking in nearly $1 billion in taxpayer dollars over the last five years.

LA REAL ESTATE VET COMES AT MAYOR BASS WITH RECEIPTS OVER DAMNING HOMELESSNESS REPORT: 'SHE DOESN'T GET IT'

"Los Angeles remains the epicenter of the nation’s drug-fueled homelessness crisis. On top of this, their failure has enabled record homelessness fraud," HUD said.

HUD Secretary Scott Turner said LAHSA had spent years funneling federal funding to organizations without proper oversight.

"Taxpayers will no longer bankroll an organization that fails to deliver for the Americans it was created to serve," Turner said in a statement.

HUD’S HOMELESSNESS REFORMS PUT HUMAN LIVES AHEAD OF HOUSING BUREAUCRACY

"For years, American taxpayers have been sending billions of dollars to Los Angeles to house the homeless and other vulnerable Americans. The result? Fraud and corruption," Scott Brady, executive director of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, added in a statement.

HUD added that it is committed to ending what it called the "harmful" "Housing First" policy, which provides permanent housing to homeless individuals without requiring them to meet preconditions such as sobriety or participation in therapy.

Under a new Treatment First approach, individuals will likely need to participate in addiction or mental health treatment and demonstrate progress toward recovery to qualify for and maintain housing assistance.

"HUD is rejecting the addiction-fueled depravity seen from LA’s Skid Row to New York’s ‘Boulevard of Broken Dreams’ and moving to Treatment First to restore lives of self-sufficiency," Turner previously said.

The settlement comes as HUD reports a 6.3% decrease in homelessness, the largest recorded decline, during the first year of Trump's administration.

"President Trump’s actions to secure the border, get criminal illegals off our streets and restore safety to our communities drove a historic decrease in homelessness," Turner previously said.

item.title: Variety recommends trans actress Hunter Schafer as next Bond girl alongside Robert Pattinson
item.description: Variety recommended trans "Euphoria" star Hunter Schafer as the next Bond girl opposite new 007 Robert Pattinson, saying the casting would "make history."
item.content:encoded:
Variety recommended transgender actress Hunter Schafer as a potential Bond girl opposite Robert Pattinson in the upcoming James Bond film on Monday, suggesting the casting could "make history."

After the "Twilight" series and "The Batman" star was announced as the latest actor to take over the role of 007, Variety published a list of 19 actresses who could play his love interest. 

The list included established Hollywood stars such as Emily Blunt and Margot Robbie, along with newer faces such as "One Battle After Another" actress Chase Infiniti and "Obsession" star Inde Navarrette.

Schafer was the only transgender actor on the list, and Variety's writers highlighted her as a potential standout.

ROBERT PATTINSON NAMED NEXT JAMES BOND

"Not only would Hunter Schafer make history as the first trans Bond girl, she’d be a damn good one," the article read.

The magazine pointed to Schafer's experience in the HBO series "Euphoria" and her role in the upcoming Prime Video series "Blade Runner 2099" as evidence of her acting credentials and potential chemistry with Pattinson.

"We could totally see Schafer and Pattinson sharing flirty banter before going head-to-head against some baddies — and just imagine the looks on that press tour!" Variety added.

IDRIS ELBA REJECTS 'WOKE' JAMES BOND CASTING PUSH, WARNS AUDIENCES 'WON'T GO FOR A BLACK MALE' IN THE ROLE

Fox News Digital reached out to Amazon MGM Studios for comment but did not immediately receive a response. 

Pattinson's casting followed years of anticipation after Daniel Craig's appearance as Bond in 2021's "No Time to Die." During that period, commentators proposed casting an actor of color or a woman as 007.

The announcement of Pattinson's casting, surprised longtime franchise fans, including Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo.

"As a huge fan of the Ian Fleming novels, Pattinson isn’t quite what I envisioned or what I think fans were hoping for," Arroyo told Fox News Digital. 

"After five Bond films with Daniel Craig in the lead, it was probably time to bring back some of the fun and charm that Pierce Brosnan and Roger Moore brought to the franchise.

"But it sounds like MGM/Amazon wants to give audiences a darker, moodier Bond — just when the public is craving a good, old-fashioned escape," he added. "We’ll see if audiences wish this new Bond to ‘Live or Let Die.’"

FORMER JAMES BOND ACTRESS PANS AMAZON FRANCHISE TAKEOVER AS 'ABSOLUTE MADNESS'

In a comment to Fox News Digital, the Media Research Center's Newsbusters executive editor Tim Graham described the article as a result of woke journalism interacting with classic Hollywood.

"They can only turn to this spin when Amazon failed to transform the James Bond character into a black woman this time around," Graham said. "We know what happened when they tried to make the ‘Ghostbusters’ an all-girl squad. Journalists should refrain from telling Hollywood how to remake the classics. But they know Hollywood is woke enough to take them seriously."

item.title: Skydiving injury leaves 24-year-old tourist stranded in Australia on medical no-fly list
item.description: Chloe Lowe of the United Kingdom says a 10,000-foot skydiving jump in Australia left her with a damaged eardrum, an infection, vertigo and a not-fit-to-fly certificate.
item.content:encoded:
A 24-year-old tourist says she's been stranded in Australia for weeks after a skydiving jump severely damaged her eardrum, leaving doctors to declare her medically unfit to fly home.

Chloe Lowe, a resident of Sheffield, United Kingdom, told the outlet NeedToKnow she's been stranded in Australia "for several weeks" after initially arriving in October for a solo birthday trip.

Days before the planned three-week trip ended, Lowe went skydiving and jumped out of a plane at 10,000 feet. She damaged her eardrum and realized that, once the adrenaline wore off, she couldn't hear.

She then sought medical treatment and learned she was bleeding behind her eardrum.

"I was given a not-fit-to-fly certificate and put on steroids," the influencer told NeedToKnow, a British publication.

After two weeks of healing, an infection threw another wrench into her plans, leaving her in more pain and experiencing more vertigo, she said.

"Turns out I now have an infection due to fluid that’s been trapped inside my ear," she said. 

"Every week I’m having to extend my accommodation, not knowing if I’ll be able to go home by the end of it or not."

In a redacted medical certificate shared by Lowe, Queensland Health officials stated that she was admitted to Cairns Base Hospital and is "not fit to fly at this time due to the health concerns."

"This was a really meaningful trip for me, as I wanted to visit the place where he sadly passed away," she said.

item.title: Pentagon detains senior US Army officer accused of spying for Russians after UK arrest
item.description: Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner was handed to U.S. military authorities after British counterterrorism police arrested him on suspicion of spying for Russia.
item.content:encoded:
A U.S. Army lieutenant colonel suspected of spying for Russia was handed over to U.S. military authorities Tuesday, days after British counterterrorism police arrested him on suspicion of violating national security laws.

Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, 41, was arrested Nov. 10 near Gloucester, England, on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service and obtaining or disclosing protected information under the United Kingdom's National Security Act.

British authorities previously said the allegations involved Russia, which the Kremlin denied any connection to.

SENIOR US ARMY SOLDIER ARRESTED IN UK ON SUSPICION OF SPYING FOR RUSSIA

The Associated Press, citing a U.S. official, reported that Tyner had not provided information to Russia.

Tyner's transfer followed consultations between British prosecutors, the U.K. attorney general's office and U.S. authorities, according to London's Metropolitan Police.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of U.K.'s Counter Terrorism Policing, said investigators referred the case to the Crown Prosecution Service, which consulted the attorney general's office and U.S. authorities before transferring the investigation.

RUSSIAN SPIES ORCHESTRATED $40K MURDER PLOT IN NATION’S CAPITAL, US ALLEGES

"These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," Taylor said in a statement.

FBI Director Kash Patel said the officer was in custody following a joint espionage investigation involving the FBI's Philadelphia field office, its London legal attaché office, British counterterrorism police, MI5, U.K. defense counterintelligence officials and U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command.

"This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk. That’s been demonstrated by the 167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests we’ve made over the last 21 months, a 53% increase," Patel said.

Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commander of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, warned service members against violating their oath to defend the Constitution.

"This case should serve as a stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath we all take to protect and defend the Constitution," Stinchon said.

Tyner, who previously deployed to Afghanistan, Iraq and Qatar, served as a senior human resources officer with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester.

The British-led multinational force, which includes personnel from 20 nations, is designed to respond rapidly to military crises and operations.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied Russian involvement following Tyner's arrest, according to the AP.

"This arrest does not concern us in any way," Peskov said Nov. 11. "We don’t know what it’s connected to. We have nothing to do with this."

British police said Tyner's arrest was unrelated to other ongoing counterterrorism investigations.

According to a Nov. 13 statement from the U.S. Army, Tyner entered active-duty service in January 2008 and deployed to Afghanistan from December 2013 to December 2014, Qatar from July 2016 to July 2017, and Iraq from December 2019 to July 2020.

item.title: Paige Spiranac leaves it all on the field, and little to the imagination, while asking NFL fans tough question
item.description: Paige Spiranac showcases a new NFL collection for Swag Golf while asking fans which team is their favorite, revealing her Steelers and Bills roots.
item.content:encoded:
There's a lot going on when Paige Spiranac drops new social media content. It's often written off as one-dimensional, but nothing could be further from the truth.

Sometimes her content is educational. Sometimes she's asking a tough question. Sometimes she does both. Most of the time her content is conversational.

There's a back-and-forth taking place that requires, at times, several views to fully grasp. Tuesday she asked NFL fans a tough question.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I admit, this doesn’t appear to be a tough question at all. She's showcasing a new NFL collection for Swag Golf while asking, "Which team is your favorite?"

All you have to do is state the name of your favorite team and off you go about your day. That is until about the third time you watch it.

What if your team isn't one of the handful Paige goes through in the video? Does it now become a question about which team of the ones she has shown is your favorite?

PAIGE SPIRANAC GIVES PEOPLE WHAT THEY DIDN'T KNOW THEY NEEDED: HER YOGURT BOWL RECIPE

By the time you figure that out, you're a half a dozen or more views in. Your mind is in a pretzel, and you try to straighten yourself back out by watching it a couple more times.

You then realize you're in too deep to turn around. You need to decide which way to go. Another time through to help you decide what you should do and, ultimately, you go with your gut.

And for everyone, that answer is going to be different. That's how Paige Spiranac asks the tough questions. She left it all out on the field on Tuesday.

As for Paige, she's supported multiple teams. Though, she has her favorites.

"Both my parents are from Pittsburgh so I was born a Steelers fan," she told her followers. "Can’t forget about my love for the Bills tho."

item.title: Steelers star says international games 'freak me out' after Aidan Hutchinson's injury in Germany
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers star Cameron Heyward said international games "freak me out" over field concerns after Aidan Hutchinson's brutal injury in Germany.
item.content:encoded:
If Pittsburgh Steelers star Cameron Heyward never played a game outside the United States again, he would be OK with it.

Heyward was asked about Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson’s brutal season-ending injury he suffered during a sack celebration in Germany on Sunday. The four-time All-Pro referenced how New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye got hurt on the same play.

"I don't like to, you know, those international games freak me out just because of that. It's just, those fields are a little bit different. It's wild to see," Heyward said during an appearance on "The Rich Eisen Show."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye, who may have suffered a season-ending ankle injury on the play, and jumped into the air to celebrate. When he landed, he grabbed his right knee and crumpled to the ground at Allianz Arena, home to FC Bayern Munich.

The seven-time Pro Bowler said he feels horrible for Hutchinson.

"Oh man, that was, as a defender, you're like, I get the sack, and then you go to celebrate, and I'm always wary about jumping in there 'cause there's freaky stuff that happens. But you know, I, I feel horrible for the kid. I got a chance to meet Aiden years ago; we were doing a Super Bowl commercial, and he's one of the nicest dudes, and a lot of respect for his family," Heyward said.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Losing Hutchinson is a major blow to the Lions' defense , which is currently without star linebacker Jack Campbell after he suffered a terrifying neck injury last month.

In nine games, Hutchinson has recorded 24 tackles and six sacks. While the Lions are 7-2 and sit atop the NFC North, the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears are also 7-2. The fourth-place Green Bay Packers are 6-4.

In such a competitive division, the Lions were relying on Hutchinson to lead their defense and help them keep pace.

Heyward would know that playing surfaces are different internationally, as the Steelers played in the NFL’s first-ever game in Paris in October, which they won 16-10 over the New Orleans Saints. The Lions-Patriots game was the final European game of the season.

The San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings will play in Mexico City on Sunday night, marking the final international game of the season.
